family.tagline: Two parents, two children, and one Companion Core on the credenza.
family.story: Linh schedules shifts at a hospital, and Duc builds cloud systems for a living. Mai, eleven, and Bao, eight, share the bunk room upstairs. One Companion Core on the living-room credenza serves all four.

companion.name: Cricket
companion.job: Fills in school and club forms from the details Linh gives it.
companion.limits: Prepares forms only. Linh reads each one and sends it.

companion.name: Ember
companion.job: Drafts short notes from the details Duc messages to it.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Duc reads every word before he sends it.

popup.title: Duc carries the parcel in
popup.body: A parcel waits on the timber steps. Inside is a Companion Core, and Duc carries it past the kitchen to the credenza.

popup.title: Unbox the Companion Core
popup.body: Inside: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. Mai reads the guide aloud, and Bao holds the cable.

popup.title: Plug it in
popup.body: At the credenza, Bao presses the button while Duc steadies the cable. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Join it from a phone
popup.body: On her phone, Linh opens the Wi-Fi settings and joins the Core's own network. Then she chooses the home network.

popup.title: Choosing the first agents and apps
popup.body: In the Companion Hub store, Linh picks OpenClaw and Duc picks Hermes. They add HomeHub, VaultWarden and Gitea, then walk away.

beats.capability: an agent with browser automation and tool use, running in a sandboxed app on your Core

popup.title: Cricket says good morning
popup.body: Cricket, the agent Linh named, answers her first greeting from the credenza. The Core is running.

say.speaker: linh
say.text: Good morning, Linh. I am Cricket. What comes first?

beats.capability: stream your own music collection to any device

popup.title: Duc picks the afternoon's music
popup.body: Afternoon light crosses the west glass. Duc picks an album from the family's own music files, and Navidrome plays it from the Core to his phone.

beats.capability: back up, search and organise your family photos and videos

popup.title: Bao finds the best ferry picture
popup.body: Bao finds last summer's best ferry picture. The family's photos sit in Immich on the Core, not in a photo cloud. The first start took a while.

beats.capability: host private Git repositories, pull requests and issues on your Core

popup.title: Duc pushes the bike script
popup.body: Duc builds cloud systems by day. On Saturday he pushes his bike script to Gitea. The repository sits on the Core, not on a rented code host.

beats.capability: talks to you through the messaging platform you pick, from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Ember drafts the landlord note
popup.body: The garage door sticks. Duc messages Ember the details. Ember drafts a note for the landlord on the Core's local model. Duc reads it and sends it himself.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: duc
say.text: Here it is, short and polite. You decide whether it goes.

beats.capability: send a push notification to your phone from any script or automation

popup.title: Duc stops forgetting the bins
popup.body: Duc forgets the bins every Thursday morning. Now an n8n workflow on the Core sends a ntfy message to his phone the afternoon before.

beats.capability: a shared household hub for shopping, chores and a recipe book

popup.title: Mai trades dishes for the table
popup.body: Beside the fridge, Mai swaps her dish-drying chore with Bao's table-laying one. The shared chore list in HomeHub lives on the Core, where both parents can read it.

beats.capability: a shared household hub for shopping, chores and a recipe book

popup.title: Bao adds eggs to the list
popup.body: The eggs have run out. At the breakfast bar, Bao adds them to the HomeHub shopping list, and Mai adds oranges. The list is served from the Core.

beats.capability: plan tasks and time blocks in one local file on your Core

popup.title: Linh's shifts move the whole week
popup.body: A new hospital rota lands on Monday. At the oval table, Linh fits the school concert around it in Companion Planning, one local file on the Core.

beats.capability: an agent with browser automation and tool use, running in a sandboxed app on your Core

popup.title: Cricket gets the trip form ready
popup.body: The school trip form is due. Linh asks Cricket to fill it in, and Cricket prepares it in its own browser. Linh reads every line before she presses send.
popup.note: OpenClaw reaches websites over your home internet.

say.speaker: linh
say.text: The form is ready. Please read it before you send it.

beats.capability: store every password in a vault you host

popup.title: Linh finds the forgotten password
popup.body: Mai forgets her reading-site password. Linh finds it in VaultWarden, a vault the family hosts on the Core. It works with the Bitwarden apps.

beats.capability: read ebooks in your browser, with bookmarks and notes, from a library on your Core

popup.title: Mai bookmarks the tides chapter
popup.body: Mai reads the tides chapter of a sea book in Koodo Reader and bookmarks the page for class. The book comes from the family's library on the Core.

beats.capability: a whiteboard with a hand-drawn look to sketch ideas together

popup.title: Bao draws the marble run first
popup.body: For the school fair, Bao draws his marble run, ramps first. Mai adds the labels, and the whiteboard runs on the Core.

beats.capability: translate text and documents on your own Core

popup.title: Mai checks a welcome sign
popup.body: A new classmate speaks Portuguese. Mai writes a welcome sign and checks it in LibreTranslate on the Core, whose language models were downloaded once.

beats.capability: send files between phones and laptops on the same Wi-Fi

popup.title: The marble run crosses the Wi-Fi
popup.body: The cardboard marble run is finished. Bao takes its picture on Linh's phone, then sends it to the family laptop with PairDrop, across the home Wi-Fi.

beats.capability: chat with models running on your own Core, from any browser

popup.title: Mai learns it to teach Bao
popup.body: Bao asks why volcanoes erupt, and Mai is not sure. She asks the model on the Core, through Open WebUI, then explains it in her own words.

beats.capability: the Obsidian note app in your browser; notes stay as local Markdown files

popup.title: The reading log gets a line
popup.body: At the laptop, Mai adds a line to her reading log: one note for each book she finishes. Obsidian saves each note as a plain Markdown file on the Core.

beats.capability: track your plants, watering and care history with photos and a garden journal

popup.title: Linh finds last year's trim date
popup.body: Last year's journal note says the low front hedge was trimmed in spring. Linh checks it in HortusFox, trims the hedge again and adds a picture.

popup.title: Four people, one Companion Core
popup.body: Passwords, code, forms and homework find a place on one Companion Core. It sits on the credenza, and the family walks past it.

closing.body: Your family's lists, passwords and homework can live on a Companion Core at home. Browse the Companion Hub store and pick your first apps.

notes: This home has no TV, bookshelf or office. The media beat sits at the couch with Navidrome and Immich on phones; Linh works at the dining table and Duc in the garage, anchored on the bicycle and the room.
Duc's garage has a workbench, cube storage and a bicycle but no laptop or desk (the only laptop is on the bunk room desk), so no beat puts a laptop in the garage.
OpenClaw (Cricket) prepares the trip form in its own browser; Linh reads it and presses send. The OpenClaw website note rides on dining-form.
Ember is Hermes: the first Hermes beat is garage-roller and carries the chat-service note. Duc sends the landlord note himself.
Companion Planning, OpenClaw and Hermes send crash reports to Companion Intelligence unless switched off. No beat says nothing leaves the Core.
LibreTranslate carries downloaded once. Koodo Reader (kids-tides): reading and a bookmark only; no look-up claim. Immich carries the slow first start. VaultWarden works with the Bitwarden apps.
ntfy: iOS push can use an upstream relay, so garage-ping makes no claim about where the message travels.
